Package neqsim.process.equipment.compressor

Class EntrainedSaltDepositSource

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.EntrainedSaltDepositSource
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, DepositSource
public class EntrainedSaltDepositSource extends Object implements DepositSource
DepositSource for salt precipitation from entrained produced water carried into a compressor.

Dissolved salt (for example NaCl) is essentially non-volatile: when entrained brine droplets enter the hot compressed gas and the water evaporates, the salt it carried precipitates as a solid that can foul the impeller. The deposition rate is therefore a mass balance: 

 salt precipitation rate = entrainedWaterRate * salinity * evaporatedFraction
 deposition rate         = salt precipitation rate * captureFraction

By default the whole entrained water load is assumed to evaporate (evaporatedFraction = 1.0), which is the conservative worst case for salt fouling. Use estimateWaterEvaporatedFraction(StreamInterface, double, double) to compute the evaporated fraction from a flash of the gas stream between the compressor inlet and discharge conditions and set it with setEvaporatedFraction(double).

This mass-balance approach avoids solid-salt electrolyte convergence issues while still tying the deposit amount to the process (entrained water rate, salinity, and how much water flashes off).

1.0
